story.title: Generated context is a representation choice
paragraphs: Self-generated documents (Self-Docs) are passages a model writes from its own parametric memory before answering. They draw on no external source; they externalize what the generator can already produce, which may make useful facts easier to use. If the source is generated rather than retrieved, which properties of that text decide whether it helps?

The paper treats the document type as an experimental variable. A detailed formal report and a conversational overview can share facts yet suit different tasks: fact verification needs specific evidence, while a long-form explanation needs coverage and organization.

mechanism.title: Generator size, document type, and mixing are tested separately
paragraphs: The experiments first separate three factors that are otherwise confounded: the size of the base model, which both writes and answers; the number of documents; and the size of the generator alone, with the answerer fixed at Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct. Documents come from GenRead's few-shot pipeline, whose examples are drawn from k-means clusters of query–document pairs.

The taxonomy, grounded in Systemic Functional Linguistics, crosses three binary choices: tone (Authoritative or Conversational), granularity (Fine- or Coarse-grained), and structure (Structured or Unstructured). Types are named by these initials: AFU is authoritative, fine-grained, and unstructured (the paper's example is a case study), CFU a personal essay, and CCU a social media post.

Finally, Direct Mix concatenates retrieved Wikipedia passages with Self-Docs, while Style-Transformation Mix first has an LLM rewrite the passages in the Self-Docs' style. Because the rewrite is itself a model step, a gain belongs to the whole pipeline, not to the retrieved content alone.

evidence.title: Style-aligned mixing helps, except on long-form answers
paragraphs: Gains are task-specific. Relative to the same documents alone, Style-Transformation Mix gains most on multi-hop HotpotQA and fact-verification FEVER and leaves long-form ELI5 essentially unchanged. Among generated types, unstructured documents beat structured ones on average, authoritative fine-grained ones suit FEVER, and conversational ones suit ELI5.

Scale effects are also uneven. A larger generator helps only above a size threshold; smaller generators struggle to beat either answering without documents or Wikipedia retrieval. More documents help FEVER, while ELI5 may plateau or dip.

demo.title: Which document type helps which task?
demo.description: Choose a tone, a granularity, and a structure to select one of the eight Self-Doc types, then choose whether the documents are used alone or mixed with Wikipedia passages. All eight types stay in the table; the second table changes one choice at a time.

dimensions.label: Tone
values: a formal style that establishes authority, as in a research paper
an engaging tone that addresses the reader, as in a blog

dimensions.label: Granularity
values: detailed information, as in a technical paper
a broader overview, as in a summary

dimensions.label: Structure
values: headings and lists that aid navigation, as in a report
continuous prose with a narrative flow, as in an essay

## Introduction
The VS-300, formally designated as the Sikorsky VS-300, is recognized as a seminal helicopter design.

AFU.excerpt: The VS-300 is a helicopter, specifically a prototype that marked a pivotal moment in the evolution of rotorcraft technology during the early 1940s.

# Overview of the VS-300
## Introduction
The VS-300 was a significant aircraft in the development of vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) technology.

ACU.excerpt: The VS-300 is a notable aircraft that stands out in the history of aviation as a significant experimental helicopter.
